item.title: Shaping black hole resonances II: Spectroscopic landscapes and interference in black hole ringdown
item.description:
arXiv:2611.13075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We map analytically the excitation of Schwarzschild quasinormal modes (QNMs) $C_n$ by oscillatory Gaussian perturbations across the pulse width $\sigma$ and carrier frequency $
u$. The excitation coefficient of each mode is determined by the product of an intrinsic excitation factor and a source-dependent overlap evaluated at the complex QNM frequency. For oscillatory Gaussian perturbations, this overlap is the coherent sum of the positive- and negative-frequency branches of the source, with its amplitude factorizing exactly into a Gaussian spectral envelope and an interference factor. We observe that the excitation amplitude peaks at $
u=\omega_n^{m Re}$ only for narrowband sources. For sufficiently broadband pulses, the maximum lies at $
u=0$, so efficient excitation does not necessarily require matching the carrier and the mode frequency. We observe that the interference between branches, modulates the amplitude only for nonzero $
u$, a feature generic to real oscillatory sources. The prominence of the interference-induced modulation is controlled by the ratio $\omega_n^{m Re}/\omega_n^{m Im}$. The phase separates into a mode-only, a width-only and a $
u$-dependent term, the last generated by the same interference, with $
u=0$ being its unique maximum at fixed width. The analytical predictions are validated against time-domain numerical simulations, showing a relative median error of $\sim 4\%$ for $|C_0|$. For $|C_1|$, the median error is $\sim 16\%$ when $\sigma\leq 5$, increasing to $\sim 36\%$ across the full parameter space. The median phase difference for $n=0$ is $\sim0.14 \,m rad $ and for $n=1$, $\sigma\leq5$ it is $0.34\,m rad$. Our results demonstrate that QNM excitation cannot be understood through frequency matching alone and may provide qualitative insights into more realistic astrophysical scenarios.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Svyatkovskyy Kholyavka, Sayak Datta, Jose Antonio Le\'on Vega, Xisco Jim\'enez Forteza

item.title: Depletion of Dark Matter Spikes by Massive Black Hole Mergers
item.description: arXiv:2611.13170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dark matter over-densities around massive black holes, known as dark matter spikes, can dephase gravitational waves emitted by intermediate- and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (IMRIs/EMRIs), offering a promising way to indirectly detect dark matter. This detection channel, however, requires the spike to survive over cosmological time-scales. We investigate the impact that a host black hole's merger history has on its dark-matter spike. We focus on how the inspiral of a massive-black-hole (MBH) binary modifies and disrupts these spikes within the central $\sim 100$ Schwarzschild radii of the black hole. We find that a single merger with mass ratio $q = 0.03$ is capable of reducing a spike's density by around 3 (5) orders of magnitude at 100 (5) Schwarzschild radii across all polar angles relative to the binary's plane, independent of the primary MBH's mass, with larger mass ratios inducing even stronger depletion. In fact, a single past merger with mass ratio as small as $q = 0.005$ reduces central densities by 2--3 orders of magnitude, making gravitational-wave dephasing difficult to detect. We relate these results to the MBH merger history by analysing cosmological simulation data from Horizon-AGN. We find that mergers become increasingly common as the MBH mass increases, with mergers of mass ratio q > 0.03 having occurred in 50% of MBHs of mass $3\times10^7M_\odot$ and 95% of mass $10^8M_\odot$ at z=0. These fractions are reached at even lighter masses ($2\times10^7M_\odot$ and $5\times10^7M_\odot$, respectively) at z=3. We find that accretion-induced adiabatic MBH growth is unable to cause appreciable spike re-growth between such mergers in {\tt Horizon-AGN}. Thus, in combination with previous studies of EMRI-induced depletion, this work constrains the mass range over which massive black holes can host detectable DM spikes to $10^6M_\odot$--$5 \times 10^7M_\odot$ for $z \leq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Sharpe, Thomas F. M. Spieksma, Yonadav Barry Ginat, Ricarda S. Beckmann, Alexander Heger, Bence Kocsis

item.title: Eccentricity greatly enhances the detectability of line-of-sight acceleration in gravitational wave signals
item.description: arXiv:2611.13197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compact object binaries formed dynamically are characterized by a tail of eccentric sources and by the potential presence of environmental perturbations. Here we show that the presence of eccentricity in a gravitational-wave (GW) signal strongly enhances the sensitivity to environmental effects, focusing in particular on line-of-sight acceleration (LSA). We demonstrate that this enhancement is recovered in Fisher-analysis forecasts and, crucially, persists in full Bayesian parameter estimation using state-of-the-art eccentric waveform models. The key insight is that the signal should be analyzed from the moment the first detectable eccentric harmonic enters the detector band, rather than from the customary entry of the $n=2$ harmonic: this allows to probe the early inspiral and thus a longer signal, over which the GW dephasing introduced by LSA becomes substantially larger. We show that with this approach constraints on LSA can increase by more than an order of magnitude between eccentricities at 20~Hz $e_{20}=0$ and $e_{20}\sim0.1$, for signals with sufficient signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR), while we predict a factor $5$ amplification even for low-SNR ones. Fully exploiting this effect necessitates the continued improvement of efficient eccentric waveform models and likelihood evaluations, enabling the efficient analysis of signals lasting thousands of seconds and containing a large number of harmonics.
item.dc:creator: J\'anos Tak\'atsy, Anna Puecher, Gonzalo Morras, Lorenz Zwick

item.title: Polarized Equatorial Emission around Kerr Black Holes with Synchronized Scalar Hair. II. Indirect images
item.description: arXiv:2611.13253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the intensity polarization properties of the indirect images of a geometrically and optically thin accretion disk around fully self-consistent models of Kerr black holes with synchronized scalar hair. The presence of a massive, self-gravitating scalar field can dramatically alter the lensing properties of the spacetime, resulting in morphologically complex indirect images. We show that for a representative high scalar charge model, this results in the presence of high order central ring-like images at low observer inclinations. These images are not exponentially demagnified, and their polarized intensity, relative to the direct images, is significant. We therefore conclude that the observational signature of strongly scalarized Kerr black holes may not be dominated solely by the $n=1$ image, as images with $n\geq2$ may also contribute significantly to the observed polarized emission, depending on the radial emissivity profile of the disk and the observer inclination.
item.dc:creator: Valentin O. Deliyski, Tsanimir Angelov, Galin N. Gyulchev, Stoytcho S. Yazadjiev

item.title: Challenging the hoop conjecture with spinning pancakes and baguettes
item.description: arXiv:2611.13266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding when gravitational collapse produces a black hole remains a central challenge in general relativity. Black-hole uniqueness results characterize the stationary endpoint under suitable assumptions, while singularity theorems establish geodesic incompleteness in the presence of trapped surfaces and appropriate energy and global conditions. Neither, however, provides a general criterion for horizon formation. The hoop conjecture offers such a criterion by relating the enclosed mass to the compactness of a matter distribution in every direction. We construct axisymmetric families of initial data describing rotating dust and test a formulation of the conjecture adapted to this setting. We explore highly prolate and oblate configurations with both constant and differential rescaled angular-velocity profiles, including configurations near the threshold for apparent-horizon formation. We find that the conjecture holds for rotating configurations, with a coefficient within 14% of unity as in the nonrotating case, provided the quasilocal mass includes the rotational energy. If the irreducible mass of the apparent horizon is used instead, the deviations grow with spin, as they do for Kerr black holes. For horizonless configurations, the conjecture likewise holds when the mass is restricted to the energy enclosed by the matter surface, whereas using the ADM mass, which also includes rotational field energy outside the matter, leads to apparent violations of up to $\approx$25%. We also discuss the possible evolution of compact configurations without apparent horizons, their relation to weak cosmic censorship, and their implications for horizonless compact objects.
item.dc:creator: Robin Croft, Gerardo Garc\'ia-Moreno, Paolo Pani

item.title: Viscosity heats, diffusion drains: Open-system thermodynamics in unimodular cosmology
item.description: arXiv:2611.13269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In GR with bulk viscosity and in unimodular gravity with energy diffusion, the matter sector is non-adiabatic, and their balance, entropy, and temperature equations match if $\Pi \leftrightarrow \dot{Q}/3H$. Disagreement over whether unimodular cosmology is adiabatic comes from assigning entropy to matter only or to the total effective fluid. The key is the temperature $T_D$ of the sector absorbing the diffused energy: comoving entropy production is $\dot{Q}(1/T_D-1/T_m)$, yielding earlier limits for $T_D \rightarrow \infty$ and $T_D \rightarrow T_m$. For finite $T_D$, diffusion acts like heat exchange with an external reservoir: unlike viscosity, which only heats a closed fluid, diffusion into a colder bath can cool an open one, breaking the viscosity-diffusion correspondence for observables and stability. Cosmographically, $\Pi$ is fixed by the deceleration $q$, while diffusion is fixed by the jerk $j$; thus $\Lambda$CDM is the adiabatic limit of unimodular cosmology but remains dissipative when modeled via viscosity. The diffusive analogue of $|\Pi|/\rho$ is the shift $c_s^2-\omega$ in effective sound speed, set by perturbative stability rather than acceleration. If dark matter is a gas with conserved rest mass, consistent diffusion removes only thermal energy, forbids phantom behavior, and bounds the growth of the cosmological term by the finite thermal reservoir; producing a logotropic dark fluid with conserved particle number would require relativistic dark matter at $z\simeq12$. With the Hayward-Kodama apparent-horizon temperature, the generalized second law in unimodular gravity follows from the local one, whereas for bulk viscosity it must be imposed separately.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Cruz, Samuel Lepe

item.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
item.description: arXiv:2611.13462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are described by second-order tensor perturbations that contain free radiation together with a gauge-dependent response maintained by the scalar source. For a perfect fluid with constant equation of state $0<w<1$, we identify the free radiation with the out-state of the tensor perturbation, assembled from the light-cone residue of kernel functions for each pair of scalar modes. Its amplitudes follow from a classical LSZ-type reduction formula, in terms of the initial data and the light-cone-projected source. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: a redefinition of the tensor perturbation whose late-time shift has power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leaves these amplitudes unchanged. Transformations between intrinsic gauges, whose slice-normal observers and spatial coordinates are fixed by the matter and geometry without an external clock or independent oscillatory dynamics, are redefinitions of this kind, except on resonance surfaces of zero measure. The out-state is therefore the same in all intrinsic gauges, including the standard gauges of cosmological perturbation theory. The late-time Newtonian kernel is then the out-state kernel, which justifies its use for the energy spectrum of the free radiation. In matter domination, the out-state instead separates the free radiation from the static tidal response.
item.dc:creator: Yizhou Lu

item.title: Quasinormal overtones and grey-body factors of Frolov black holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.13569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate scalar quasinormal modes (QNMs), with particular attention to overtones, and grey-body factors of Frolov black holes, which interpolate between the Reissner--Nordstr\"om (RN) and Hayward limits. Over the allowed ranges of charge $q$ and regularization parameter $\alpha_0$, all QNM frequencies have negative imaginary parts, confirming stability against scalar perturbations. Increasing either $q$ or $\alpha_0$ can trigger overtone outbursts, with the Frolov threshold shifted to smaller parameter values than in the RN or Hayward cases. Angular momentum does not eliminate the outburst but postpones its onset from $n=1$ at $l=0$ to $n\geq 2$ at $l=1$. Comparisons of the effective potential show that, for $l=1$, charge raises the barrier peak much more strongly than $\alpha_0$, while the clearest deviations from the Hayward and RN references are localized near the horizon. Using the QNM--grey-body correspondence at $l=1$, we find that overtone corrections are essential, and the amended formula substantially outperforms the eikonal truncation. At fixed frequency, both $q$ and $\alpha_0$ suppress transmission, with charge being the dominant factor, consistent with the stronger barrier enhancement under the charge scan.
item.dc:creator: Ying Huang, Huajie Gong, Li-Gang Zhu, Jian-Pin Wu

item.title: Inverse Scattering & Isospectrality in (Analog) Cosmology
item.description: arXiv:2611.13871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cosmological particle production, the excitation of field quanta by a dynamical spacetime, underlies the primordial perturbations observed in the cosmic microwave background and has been realized in analog quantum simulators with ultra-cold atoms. We ask the inverse question: given the excitation spectrum, can the cosmological history that produced it be reconstructed, and is that reconstruction unique? We approach this problem through a mapping of particle production to one-dimensional quantum scattering, in which the expansion history plays the role of a scattering landscape and the produced spectrum the role of reflected and transmitted waves. This mapping reveals a rich interplay between scattering theory and cosmology. The scale factor enters as a zero-energy resonance, an exceptional case of scattering theory, while cosmic singularities correspond to bound states, so that regular cosmologies are governed entirely by the scattering continuum. We find an interesting isospectrality: histories related by an inversion of the scale factor (expansion <-> contraction) yield identical particle numbers, differing only by a pi-shift in phase. Given both the particle number (or alternatively the amplitude) and phase of the cosmological power spectrum, the reconstruction is unique for regular, asymptotically static cosmologies. We demonstrate the reconstruction both analytically, for exactly solvable scattering landscapes, and numerically, recovering common logistic expansion histories to better than 0.02%. We further quantify its robustness to the momentum-space resolution and measurement uncertainties characteristic of analog quantum simulation. This work establishes a direct link between the observable power spectrum and the cosmological history that produced it, offering a new perspective on the classification of early-universe scenarios and the construction of alternatives to inflation.
item.dc:creator: Christian F. Schmidt, Stefan Floerchinger

item.title: Non-singular cosmology from effective LQG-inspired black holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.14001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a non-singular primordial cosmology derived from matching an effective Loop Quantum Gravity-inspired black hole geometry to an expanding Friedmann-Lema\^{i}tre-Robertson-Walker universe via Darmois-Israel junction conditions. The resulting modified Friedmann equation replaces the singularity with a quantum bounce in the Planckian regime. Mapping the surface energy-momentum tensor of the dynamic thin shell onto a homogeneous scalar field reveals a transient phantom-like behavior. For any equation of state of the shell satisfying $\omega > -1$, its effective energy density is diluted with cosmic expansion. Extending the framework to a two-scalar-field system provides a mechanism to bridge the energy gap between the Planckian bounce and the sub-Planckian scale. The pre-inflationary phase is brief, enabling the second scalar field to take over to drive the standard slow-roll inflation.
item.dc:creator: V. F. C. Belo, F. G. S. Menezes, S. M. Rupf, I. P. R. Baranov, H. A. Borges

item.title: Gravitational Origin of Black Hole Thermodynamic Geometry from Boundary Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2611.14031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In black hole thermodynamics, Hessian metrics change both their signature and their singularities from one statistical ensemble to another. A negative eigenvalue may therefore signal either a physical instability or only a Legendre transformation. We derive this geometry from the bulk action and boundary terms of four-dimensional Euclidean Einstein-Maxwell-anti-de Sitter gravity. In the bulk, the radial symplectic flux pairs the mass and charge with their asymptotic sources, and horizon regularity selects the equilibrium states. At infinity, the boundary terms determine the ensemble polarization by specifying which reservoir parameters are held constant and which conjugate quantities fluctuate. Fixing the temperature and electric potential gives the Ruppeiner metric, whereas adding the Maxwell boundary term fixes the charge and reverses the corresponding metric sign. Tracking the boundary conditions thus separates true stability boundaries from singularities of the Legendre transform. Local holographic counterterms leave the metric unchanged, while mixed electric boundary conditions interpolate between the two ensembles and shift their stability limits.
item.dc:creator: Ling-Zheng Xia, Lixin Xu

item.title: Renormalized dynamical tidal response of neutron stars in binary dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.14077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the relativistic dynamical tidal response of a neutron star computed using stellar perturbation theory and matched to a worldline effective field theory via the tidal scattering phase. This phase is defined as the difference between the Compton/Raman scattering phase of gravitational-waves from a neutron star and the real part of the black hole scattering phase. The gravitational corrections to the response function are obtained using self-energy corrections up to fourth post-Minkowskian order. The response function for neutron stars obeying the BSk22 equation-of-state from Brussels-Skyrme family, is then consistently matched to an effective theory of relativistic quadrupolar harmonic oscillators to model the fundamental-mode ($f$-mode) and low-frequency gravity-modes ($g$-modes). This matching includes the frequency and tidal coupling of each mode and the post-adiabatic dynamical tidal Love number, and once matched this model is in excellent agreement with the full neutron star response. With the external tidal field up to third post-Newtonian order, we also analyse the tidal coupling of the induced quadrupole on the neutron star in a circular binary system, and the adiabatic binding energy.
item.dc:creator: M. V. S. Saketh, Raj Patil, Godwin Martin, Nils Andersson, Suprovo Ghosh, Jan Steinhoff

item.title: Response of Circular Binaries to Monochromatic Gravitational Waves
item.description: arXiv:2611.14151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The exchange in specific orbital energy between a test particle in a Keplerian binary orbit and a continuously incident linearized gravitational wave (GW) is considered. Analytical expressions for the rate of change of energy, semi-major axis and mean motion of the test particle are derived. Numerical solutions illustrate a resonance effect betwen the GWs frequency and the particle's initial orbital frequency. We distinguish between bounded short-period oscillations and resonant libration. The effect of the GWs angle of incidence with the particle's orbital plane is also considered. Using an illustrative high GW strain we show that changes to the eccentricity are bounded while inclination exhibits small linear growth for an initially flat, circular orbit. Long coherence requirements linit the observational significance of GW resonance to astrophysical systems with very short orbital periods.
item.dc:creator: Corey McInerney, Phil J. Sutton

item.title: Search Method for Continuous Gravitational Waves from Rotating Neutron Stars in Highly Eccentric Wide Orbits
item.description: arXiv:2611.14197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent results from the Gaia third data release have highlighted 21 potential neutron stars candidates in wide, highly-eccentric binary systems and provide estimates of their orbital parameters. We present a feasibility study for a directed search for continuous gravitational waves (CWs) tailored for these and similar systems. To this extent, we have computed a frequency metric to place templates in the parameter space accounting for uncertainties on the orbital parameters. We have built upon the FastTracks infrastructure to efficiently tackle the high-dimensional search space, leveraging a combination of downsampling and interpolation to reduce the computational cost of generating the binary Doppler correction. We performed an injection campaign to demonstrate the performance of this procedure and showed that a search using this approach is viable. Such a search would represent the first combination of Gaia observations and CW analysis.
item.dc:creator: M. Ball, S. Bussi\`eres, L. Mirasola, J. R. Merou, A. K. Sharma, N. Singh, D. Keitel, A. M. Sintes

item.title: Stellar Scalar Monopoles from Gauss--Bonnet Curvature beyond Four Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.14212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Above four dimensions every static, spherically symmetric star, isotropic or anisotropic, carries a scalar monopole at first order in a scalar--Gauss--Bonnet coupling, given by an interior integral weighted by the energy density plus radial pressure. Under the radial null energy condition its sign is that of the coupling for any equation of state, opposite to that of a Schwarzschild--Tangherlini black hole at the same order. The charge is fixed by the lapse-weighted Gauss--Bonnet curvature of space, which vanishes identically when space is three-dimensional.
item.dc:creator: Sudan Hansraj

item.title: Simulation-Based Inference on EMRI Frequency Tracks: Harmonic Identification and Parameter Constraints from Search Outputs
item.description: arXiv:2611.14255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRIs) are key targets for the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, but their long, multi-harmonic waveforms make search and parameter estimation computationally expensive. A promising alternative is to work directly with frequency tracks recovered by a time-frequency search pipeline. We investigate whether such tracks can be used to (i) identify which harmonic(s) a recovered track corresponds to, and (ii) constrain the intrinsic EMRI parameters, including when tracks are partially masked near plunge. We first train Simulation-Based Inference (SBI) networks on large banks of azimuthal and radial fundamental-frequency tracks. For harmonic identification, we combine pairs of candidate tracks under different harmonic-label assumptions and use the resulting posterior medians and network acceptance rates to classify the correct labelling. For parameter identification, we apply a sequential (truncated-prior) SBI scheme and refine the results by cross-checking posterior samples against a time-frequency detection statistic. The correct harmonic pair is among the top-2 ranked candidates with probability $>0.99$ across masking levels, and is identified outright in 98% of cases when restricted to physically plausible candidates. Sequential SBI shrinks the intrinsic-parameter prior volume by up to $10^{13}$ within a few hours of GPU time, and the detection-statistic refinement reduces it by up to four further orders of magnitude, even for heavily masked tracks. Frequency-track-based SBI thus provides a fast, waveform-free way to identify EMRI harmonics and obtain tight prior volumes for targeted follow-up, substantially reducing the burden on subsequent MCMC-based analyses.
item.dc:creator: Federico Fantoccoli, Lorenzo Speri, Bert Depoorter, Jonathan R. Gair

item.title: Can torsion mimic a cosmological constant? A one-parameter logarithmic $f(T)$ extension of $\Lambda$CDM
item.description: arXiv:2611.14305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a modified teleparallel gravity model of the $f(T)$ type. We propose a new functional form for in order to obtain a geometric origin to the $\Lambda CDM$ behavior in an appropriate limit. A perturbative expansion around the $\Lambda CDM$ regime is carried out, and the model's cosmic dynamics are calculated inside the flat FLRW background. By employing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis using multiple observational datasets, such as Cosmic Chronometers, Type Ia Supernova compilations (DES-SN5YR, Pantheon+SH0ES, and Union 3.0), DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and Planck 2018 CMB distance priors, to constrain the model parameters. The findings show that the suggested $f(T)$ model accurately replicates the observed accelerated expansion and is statistically consistent with current cosmological observations. The model stays close to the $\Lambda CDM$ scenario while permitting tiny dynamical adjustments, as evidenced by the extra parameter $\gamma$, which quantifies deviations from the conventional cosmological model, being limited to values near zero.
item.dc:creator: Adriel O. Aquino, J. E. G. Silva

item.title: Images of Regular Black Holes with Hedgehog Scalar Hair Embedded in Radiatively Inefficient Accretion Flows
item.description: arXiv:2611.14306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How a black hole's geometric critical scale manifests in an accretion-flow image is governed by photon propagation, plasma radiative processes, and instrumental resolution. In this work, we investigate radiatively inefficient accretion flows (RIAF) surrounding geometrically regular black holes with hedgehog scalar hair. Adopting the mass and distance of $\mathrm{M87}^*$, we generate total-intensity synchrotron images and systematically explore the viewing inclination, disk thickness, and observing frequency. For the fiducial setup at $230\,\mathrm{GHz}$, raising $L/M$ from $0$ to $0.9$ contracts the critical curve diameter by $4.78\%$, shrinks the half-flux radius by $4.07\%$, and lowers the required electron-density scale by $9.15\%$. At $84\,\mathrm{GHz}$, the primary brightness peaks shift farther outside the critical curve due to enhanced synchrotron self-absorption, whereas the sharper emission rings at $230$ and $345\,\mathrm{GHz}$ closely trace the critical curve. Ultimately, we find that although the regular core systematically contracts the emission ring and alters the required plasma density, resolving these deviations from a Schwarzschild black hole demands angular resolution finer than that achievable with current baselines.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Shi, Hao Wei

item.title: Dynamical obstructions to primary Proca hair and its logarithmic Maxwell continuation
item.description: arXiv:2611.14344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the dynamical admissibility of primary black hole hair in a regularized vector theory of Gauss--Bonnet gravity. The original nontrivial constant norm family cannot satisfy both positive dipole kinetic energy and real nondegenerate radial tensor characteristics. A regular Hamiltonian reduction treats the degenerate boundaries. For asymptotically flat exteriors on the nondegenerate radial branch, adding a Maxwell term for the same vector requires a varying norm. Its positive logarithmic continuation has finite mass at spatial infinity and numerically constructed regular future horizons. The constructed backgrounds satisfy the radial tensor and transverse vector conditions at the sampled points. However, the constrained even angular system has a longitudinal mode with negative squared angular speed. We derive its inverse logarithm coefficient, including both the vector constraint and quartic interaction, and verify it using independent gauge reductions and the full backgrounds. This local angular obstruction persists despite the compatible radial conditions.
item.dc:creator: Anirudh Pradhan, K. Ghaderi, Ulug'bek Eshkarayev, Sardor Sabirov, Javlon Rayimbaev

item.title: Black Holes beyond General Relativity: The Effective Metric Description
item.description: arXiv:2611.14353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Black holes provide a privileged window on gravity in the strong-field regime, and deviations from the classical solutions of General Relativity (GR) may encode information about quantum gravity and other extensions of the theory. The abundance of proposed deformed black hole geometries, however, makes model-by-model comparison with observations impractical. This review presents a unified account of the Effective Metric Description (EMD), a model-independent framework in which deformations of static, spherically symmetric black hole spacetimes are parametrized by physical, coordinate-invariant quantities, such as the proper radial distance from the event horizon or the proper time of a free-falling observer. After reviewing the classical black hole solutions and the open issues that motivate going beyond GR, we develop the EMD as a series expansion near the horizon for a given physical quantity. We provide the general solution of the resulting self-consistency conditions compatible with the symmetries of the geometry, derive universal regularity conditions ensuring a finite Hawking temperature and curvature invariants, establish the equivalence of descriptions based on different physical quantities, and extend the framework to charged, extremal and lower-dimensional black holes. Pad\'e resummation extends the description away from the horizon, enabling model-independent computations of the black hole shadow and, in the eikonal limit, of quasi-normal mode frequencies in the test-field approximation. The framework is tested on a broad set of geometries used to model physics beyond GR, and compared with other model-independent parametrizations through explicit transformation maps. As an effective description of deformations beyond GR, the EMD provides a coherent bridge between fundamental black hole physics, quantum-gravity-inspired deformations, and astrophysical observables.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Del Piano, Stefan Hohenegger, Francesco Sannino

item.title: Gravitational radiation from a particle in circular orbit around a wormhole: the nonrotating case
item.description: arXiv:2611.14455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we have generalized Poisson's(1993) calculation for the case of gravitational radiation from a particle in a circular orbit around a black hole to the case of the wormhole. Considering the motion of a test particle around a Schwarzschild like wormhole and using Teukolsky formalism, we have obtained an analytical result of flux at infinity under the assumption of small velocities. Focusing on the 22-mode, we have found a novel 0.5PN order term beyond the quadrupole order, which vanishes in the black hole limit. On the other hand, all higher order terms are getting modified in such a way that they give correct correspondence in the black hole limit. We have further corroborated our results with the numerical investigations, which show that the two waveforms match well when the particle lies far from ISCO. Thus, our work provides one of the first attempts toward the study of the post-Newtonian waveforms involving wormholes (ECOs).
item.dc:creator: Shauvik Biswas, Sayan Chakrabarti

item.title: Singustars: Between Black Holes and Compact Stars
item.description: arXiv:2611.14482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equations admit singular solutions in which a negative point mass is surrounded by a self-gravitating fluid. For a $\Gamma$-law polytropic equation of state, these solutions, which we call singustars, are thick shells bounded by two zero-pressure surfaces around a naked, repulsive, negative-mass singularity, with a Schwarzschild exterior. They form a two-parameter family, labeled by the mass $M$ and the compactness $C\equiv M/R$. Singustars join regular polytropes as the central negative mass vanishes and reach compactness beyond the Buchdahl bound. From exact equilibria and their radial modes, we find that singustars with $\Gamma = 2$ are stable only for $M\lesssim0.63$ and $C\lesssim0.25$, a region that nonetheless contains configurations more compact than any stable regular polytrope, although none with a light ring. In the numerically resolved parameter space, unstable singustars have a single unstable radial mode; many are energetically unbound. Nonlinear evolutions in ingoing null coordinates show that the end state depends on the perturbation. For the collapsing models studied, backward tracing of outgoing null rays identifies an event-horizon generator with a past endpoint on the singularity, before the first trapped surface appears. Outward perturbations disperse unbound shells and leave the singularity naked, while a bound shell migrates toward, and oscillates about, a stable configuration with the same conserved masses.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Laguna

item.title: Viable Phantom Crossing in Softly Broken Shift Symmetric Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.07035v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We demonstrate a viable fit to current cosmological data from a simple Horndeski modified gravity theory that softly breaks shift symmetry. This SBSS model crosses the phantom divide $w=-1$ at $z\approx0.5$ and fits observational data (baryon acoustic oscillations and supernova distances, and cosmic microwave background power spectra) better than $w_0w_a$CDM, by $\Delta\chi^2\approx-3$ for the same number of effective parameters, while providing a physical foundation for cosmic acceleration. The theory is healthy, has no cosmological constant or potential, and has substantial protection against high energy quantum loop corrections.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Calderon, Eric V. Linder

item.title: First results from a borehole network for the seismic characterization of the Einstein Telescope Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site
item.description: arXiv:2611.12917v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The low-frequency sensitivity of the Einstein Telescope depends on the seismic environment of its site, both through the mechanical coupling of ground motion to the test masses and through Newtonian noise. We present the first results of the seismic characterization of the Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site based on a network of recently instrumented boreholes covering the first seven months of 2026 at four underground stations and their co-located surface sensors. Two of these boreholes were deliberately sited next to railway infrastructure, so that the levels reported here describe how anthropogenic transients propagate to depth at different distances from the source. The analysis was carried out with \texttt{SiteChar}, a Python framework developed for this work to provide a common processing pipeline across different sensors, networks and observation periods. It processes the data in sequential chunks and separates the noise floor from the contribution of transients. We present a characterization of the catalogue of observed transients and a tentative classification. These measurements form part of an integrated site characterization approach that combines the observed seismic field with three-dimensional geological and wave-propagation models to predict Newtonian noise and ultimately guide its mitigation at the Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site.
item.dc:creator: L. D'Onofrio, S. Koley, P. Barneo, S. Bentvelsen, S. Danilishin, G. Degrande, S. Francois, S. Kadmiel, M. Kiehn, H. Michel, F. Nguyen, T. Niggemann, N. Nippe, J. Pretz, V. Tempel, B. Vink, W. Walk

item.title: Time Running Backwards, and Where It Stops: Superoscillations of Proper Time and the Memory of the Environment
item.description: arXiv:2611.12971v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A quantum system prepared in a superposition of proper times - a clock whose worldline is superposed, or a clock at rest in a superposed gravitational potential - evolves, in each branch, by the same dynamics for a different duration. Post-selecting the control that sets the proper time turns the superposition into a superoscillation of the time-dilation factor: the system is found to have evolved for a proper time $\alpha_w t$, where the weak value $\alpha_w$ may exceed unity, vanish, or be negative - the quantum time-translation machine of Aharonov, Anandan, Popescu and Vaidman. We ask how far back such a machine can run an irreversible process. The test system is a sealed cell - excited atoms, the radiation field they emit into, and the absorbing walls, carried as one quantum object - and the witness is projective: atoms that had begun to decay before the run are found, in the post-selected sub-ensemble, more excited than when inserted. The answer is exact and depends only on the atoms' survival amplitude. With two branches the witness holds only while the decay is younger than the memory time of the environment, after which the emission becomes Markovian. Beyond it, the post-selection amplifies the minute difference between the contents of the cell in the two branches, set by the full energy spread of the atoms and their field rather than by the linewidth, and the witness fails. Reversing a decay past the memory time requires many branches, an environment with a strictly bounded spectrum, and a post-selection probability that falls exponentially with the number of environmental oscillations to be undone. The obstacle to reversal is therefore not entropy but bandwidth - the same bandwidth that makes the emission irreversible in the first place. We give four ways to superpose a clock rate, from hollow massive shells to inertial velocities.
item.dc:creator: Yakir Aharonov, Avshalom C. Elitzur

item.title: Four-charge Rotating AdS Black Holes in Gauged STU Supergravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.13074v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present an exact solutions for non-extremal rotating AdS black holes with four independent charges in four-dimensional gauged STU supergravity. The scalar potential introduced by gauging breaks the hidden symmetry underlying solution-generating methods in the ungauged theory, making the construction of such solutions a longstanding challenge. We analyse the global properties of the solution and derive its thermodynamic quantities. We further take the BPS limit and show that the resulting entropy agrees with the known microscopic result obtained from the dual conformal field theory.
item.dc:creator: Liang Ma, H. Lu

item.title: Thermal damping of spectator scalar dark matter: Relaxing the overclosure and isocurvature bounds
item.description: arXiv:2611.13080v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A light scalar present during inflation generically acquires a misalignment and can later constitute the dark matter. Since it fluctuates independently of the inflaton, however, it carries isocurvature perturbations. Isocurvature and overclosure bounds together rule out the simplest version of this scenario at high inflationary scales. We show that a weak coupling to the primordial plasma can relax both bounds simultaneously. The plasma depletes the scalar abundance through thermal damping, a dissipative effect arising from the plasma's finite equilibration time, thereby relaxing the overclosure bound. If the damping grows with the oscillation amplitude, it can also drive different initial amplitudes onto a common attractor that depends only on the local radiation temperature. This synchronizes the scalar with the adiabatic clock, thus suppressing its isocurvature. The resulting isocurvature bound on the inflationary scale relaxes by exactly the factor by which damping reduces the abundance, in addition to the relaxation from the larger initial misalignment now allowed. This result holds for any damping rate quadratic in the amplitude, regardless of its temperature dependence.
item.dc:creator: Erwin H. Tanin, Sarunas Verner

item.title: Holographic Drag Force and the Entanglement Membrane: Geometric Reconstruction and Information Spreading
item.description: arXiv:2611.13088v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A central question in holography is how different boundary observables encode and reconstruct the geometry of the gravitational dual. In this work, we uncover an exact geometric correspondence between two seemingly distinct aspects of strongly coupled dynamics: the dissipative drag force experienced by a moving heavy particle(quark) and the entanglement membrane governing the propagation of quantum information. We show that both constructions retain the same underlying structure of the geometry, leading to an invertible transformation between the finite-velocity drag force and the geometric membrane tension. This correspondence reveals that nonlinear momentum loss encodes detailed information about entanglement dynamics: the leading nonlinear correction determines the butterfly velocity, while higher-order terms successively probe the local geometry of the membrane near the horizon. We further connect this hierarchy to scalar pole-skipping, establishing an all-order relation between nonlinear dissipation and near-horizon spectral data. The shared geometric structure also has implications for quantum information recovery, with the quintic drag coefficient determining the leading dependence of information velocity on initial entanglement. Conversely, the complete information-velocity curve provides a reconstruction of the reduced bulk geometry along the physical interior membrane branch, complementing the exterior reconstruction from drag. We show that stochastic momentum broadening supplies the additional radial information needed to reconstruct the complete exterior metric up to an overall scale. Our results thus reveal how dissipation, entanglement dynamics, and spectral properties provide complementary access to holographic geometry, establishing a unified framework for understanding the geometric information encoded in distinct boundary observables.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry S. Ageev

item.title: Fast Scrambling Cosmology
item.description: arXiv:2611.13100v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum gravity arguments such as trans-Planckian censorship suggest that de Sitter space can only last for a time of order $H^{-1}\ln(M_{\rm Pl}/H)$, corresponding to the fast-scrambling time of black hole and cosmological horizons. We ask whether this clock leaves an imprint on cosmic expansion, via a minimal modification of the Raychaudhuri equation that adds a term $-\Gamma H^2/\ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)$ to $\dot H$, with $\Gamma={\cal O}(1)$. The slowly varying $\sigma\equiv\Gamma/\ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)\ll 1$ is nearly constant at late times. De Sitter space is replaced by a slowly evolving vacuum (an exact Lambert-$W$ solution), and for constant $\sigma$ the expansion rate is found in closed form for arbitrary matter sources. The correction acts as dark energy with two components: a vacuum mode with $w=-1+2\sigma/3$, and a term that integrates over the history of the cosmic fluids, so that any change in the equation of state of a species leaves a permanent residual; e.g., neutrinos becoming non-relativistic shift the dark energy density by ${\cal O}(\sigma m_\nu^4)$. A covariant clock-field completion reproduces this background, and a term that rescales the gravitational constant governing cosmic expansion removes its short-wavelength instability in the dark-energy era. Big Bang nucleosynthesis constraints give a proxy bound $\Gamma=-3.7\pm6.1$ (68% confidence), while the negative-$\Gamma$ branch qualitatively follows the $w_0w_a$CDM dark energy evolution inferred from DESI DR2 at $z\gtrsim1$. The early-time tracking terms amount to a similar rescaling, for which existing fits to cosmic microwave background (CMB), baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) and supernova data translate into the proxy estimate $\Gamma\simeq-2.8\pm0.9$ ($\sigma\simeq-0.01$ today). These background-level results motivate a dedicated likelihood analysis of structure formation in this theory.
item.dc:creator: Aliv Sahoo, Fatima Abbasi, Jake McNaughton, Niayesh Afshordi

item.title: Effective scalar-fluid description of thermal first-order phase transitions and their spinodal instabilities
item.description: arXiv:2611.13102v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate an improved scalar-fluid effective description of first-order phase transitions in relativistic theories, and test it against a microscopic calculation in a holographic model. The effective theory shows that the nature of the spinodal instability is linked to thermodynamic stability, determined by the sign of the specific heat. When the specific heat is positive, the sound modes are stable and there is a non-hydrodynamic instability. When it is negative, a sound mode becomes unstable instead. The holographic calculation confirms the validity of the effective description at long wavelengths, improving on the purely hydrodynamic description. We also identify a friction coefficient that governs the bubble wall velocity and can be extracted from a holographic correlator.
item.dc:creator: Alessio Caddeo, Oscar Henriksson, Carlos Hoyos, Mikel Sanchez-Garitaonandia, Pedro Taranc\'on-\'Alvarez

item.title: Galaxy clusters as cosmic lenses for high frequency gravitational-waves
item.description: arXiv:2611.13105v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High-frequency Gravitational Waves (HFGW)($f \gtrsim 1$ MHz) offer a distinctive probe of exotic physics. In the absence of dedicated detectors targeting this frequency range, indirect probes based on graviton-photon conversions in astrophysical magnetic fields become particularly relevant. In this work we show that the extended magnetic fields permeating Galaxy Clusters may act as cosmic lenses, leading to a strong enhancement of graviton-photon conversions. In this context, X- and $\gamma$-ray observations of the Virgo Cluster through large field-of-view instruments such as eROSITA and COMPTEL yield novel limits on the amplitude of stochastic HFGW backgrounds in the frequency range $10^{17}-10^{22}$ Hz, improving upon constraints derived from the Galactic magnetic field by one to two orders of magnitude.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Lecce, Francisco R. Cand\`on, Alessandro Lella, Alessandro Mirizzi, Julia K. Vogel, Tiziano Zanzarella

item.title: Accretion variability as a probe of black holes and their environments: Light curve signatures of a single hot spot
item.description: arXiv:2611.13109v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The compact radio source at the centre of the Milky Way, Sagittarius A*, exhibits temporal broadband brightness variability. The observed timescales of such fluctuations, ranging from minutes to hours on horizon scales, arise from the complex interplay of gravitation, plasma, and light propagation processes in the immediate vicinity of the supermassive black hole. Kinetic and fluid simulations associate this variability with turbulence and the formation of magnetised, localised plasma structures. Focusing on a single fluctuating compact emission region, a 'hot spot', we study how intrinsic source fluctuations map onto different regions of the observer's screen. Our aim is to identify distinct imprints of light propagation effects, which encode information both about the source and the underlying space-time geometry. We simulate image time series by propagating the emitted light to a distant observer's sky plane in Minkowski, Schwarzschild, and Kerr space-times. We then compute the corresponding observed light curves and power spectra, both for the full observed images and for selected angular sectors of the observer's sky plane. We derive a semi-analytical model for the power spectrum of a fluctuating hot spot in flat space-time, reproducing all qualitative features of curved-space-time spectra at moderate inclinations. Moreover, we describe how such power spectra are affected by space-time geometry, inclination, and source velocity, and show that orthogonal two-sector angular decompositions of the sky plane provide information on system orientation and lensing effects. The physical effects highlighted in this paper are expected to be present in the timing signature of accretion-flow variability, as observed by current instruments and future photometric and interferometric facilities. Further work is needed to investigate if our conclusions hold for realistic disc configurations.
item.dc:creator: I. Urso, C. Deffayet, A. Held, F. H. Vincent

item.title: Resummations In Higher-Curvature Modifications Of Starobinsky Inflation
item.description: arXiv:2611.13112v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study higher-curvature corrections to Starobinsky inflation, which are expected to be generated at the quantum level. When treated perturbatively in the couplings $\gamma$ of the higher-dimensional operators, these terms produce inverse powers of the slow-roll parameter $\alpha$, casting doubt on the reliability of the slow-roll expansion. If instead $\gamma$ is kept exact, the expansion fails to reproduce the Starobinsky model smoothly as $\gamma\to 0$. We show that this problem is solved by resumming certain series in the ratio $\alpha/\gamma$. The resulting ``improved'' slow-roll expansion is regular in the limit $\gamma\to 0$ and gives the same result whether one expands first in $\gamma$ or in $\alpha$. We illustrate this explicitly for an $R^3$ term, obtain the power spectra, spectral indices and tensor-to-scalar ratio at next-to-leading order in the improved expansion, and show that results in the recent literature are recovered as the first-order Taylor expansion of ours. Comparing with the latest ACT, Planck and SPT data, we find that the resummed and first-order results differ appreciably only for values of $n_s$ outside the favored regions. Finally, we comment on the origin of higher-curvature operators in UV-complete theories, such as renormalizable quantum gravity, where the predictions of the Starobinsky model are stable.
item.dc:creator: Marco Piva

item.title: Rotational instability and quadrupolar order in BFSS matrix theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.13122v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the effect of angular momentum on thermal states of the BFSS matrix theory in its gravitational and high-temperature classical regimes. We focus on ensembles with only one non-zero angular momentum. On the gravity side, the rotating ensemble is described by the singly-spinning D$0$ black hole. Beyond a critical rotation, we find that this solution becomes unstable to a non-axisymmetric quadrupolar perturbation. Following this mode non-linearly, we find a new branch of non-axisymmetric rotating black holes that is thermodynamically favoured over the axisymmetric branch in both the microcanonical and canonical ensembles. On the other hand, in the classical matrix limit, we find no evidence for such collective quadrupolar order over the matrix sizes and angular momenta studied. Instead, rotation accelerates the separation of a single D$0$-brane from the clump of branes initially prepared. The separated brane carries a large fraction of the angular momentum by orbiting the rest of the clump at a large in-plane radius. Both the angular momentum share and the orbital radius relative to the clump size increase with the matrix size. These results distinguish a collective quadrupolar deformation in the gravity limit from angular-momentum transfer to a single brane in the classical matrix limit.
item.dc:creator: Jun Liu, Jorge E. Santos

item.title: General non-extremal rotating charged AdS black hole solutions with four independent charge parameters in $D=4$, STU gauged supergravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.13151v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present an exact solution for generic non-extremal rotating, charged black holes with a negative cosmological constant in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2, U(1)^4$ gauged supergravity. This general non-extremal solution contains seven independent parameters related to the mass, rotation, two electric and two magnetic charges, as well as a nonzero cosmological constant. It generalizes the four-dimensional Cveti\v{c}-Youm black hole solution to the gauged supergravity case. We anticipate that this is the only regular black hole solution in four-dimensional gauged STU model without any Misner string singularity and/or C-metric-like conical defect on the symmetry axes. We also investigate its thermodynamic property and give the Killing-St\"ackel tensor responsible for the separability of Hamilton-Jacobi and massless Klein-Gordon equations. Various special cases related to the known solution are discussed, and its BPS limit is also analyzed. Our solution provides a new background to test the AdS$_4$/CFT$_3$ correspondence and to study the microscopic entropy via extremization of the BPS index.
item.dc:creator: Di Wu, Shuang-Qing Wu

item.title: Expiscating the black hole singularity in holography
item.description: arXiv:2611.13261v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We argue that the leading exponential rate in the high frequency asymptotics of holographic thermal two-point functions is independent of the conformal dimension and spin (held fixed) of the operator. We analyze the leading universal WKB spectral curve governing the asymptotics at non-vanishing momentum scaling with frequency. We show that its classical action governs time domain signatures of the bouncing geodesic singularity, highly damped quasinormal modes, and the asymptotics of multi-stress tensor OPE coefficients. Beyond the leading order, we examine linear and dimension-dependent sublinear scalings of momentum with frequency. In both regimes, we derive the connection matrix between the boundary and the horizon using exact-WKB techniques. The results show a factorization of the spectral function into a perturbative part controlled by the OPE and a non-perturbative part governed by WKB transport. For linear scaling at fixed $k/\omega$ in the timelike regime, the turning points controlling physical transport remain separated from the curvature singularity. Nevertheless, a singularity-anchored representative of the same transport homology class determines the leading WKB action. In the sublinear regime, the relevant turning points approach the singularity. We match an exact solution of the near-singularity scaled equation to the exterior WKB solution to determine the connection matrix and spectral function. Our results clarify how the black hole curvature singularity is encoded in dual field theory observables at leading order in the planar expansion.
item.dc:creator: Hewei Frederic Jia, Mukund Rangamani

item.title: A dual-moment framework toward unification of the four fundamental interactions
item.description: arXiv:2611.13418v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The unification of the four fundamental interactions remains one of the central open challenges in fundamental physics. Most existing unification scenarios rely on extra spatial dimensions, novel symmetry structures, or unobserved dynamical degrees of freedom. In this work, we construct a minimal phenomenological dual-moment framework rooted in primitive charges and motion-induced kinetic moments. Gravitational, electromagnetic, and strong interactions are coherently described within a unified inverse-square-law formalism. We postulate a universal coupling relation $T = Z/c^2$ that connects source-charge coupling coefficients and moment-mediated coupling coefficients across different interaction sectors. While the framework can formally accommodate weak-charge degrees of freedom, full quantitative computations for weak-interaction dynamics are deferred to future follow-up studies. The model reproduces established low-energy dynamical limits for planetary orbits, atomic systems, and heavy-quark hadrons, and predicts distinguishable corrections to light deflection by rapidly spinning compact objects. We further design three independent test schemes: improved torsion-balance measurements, a mass-current laboratory deflection experiment, and astronomical light-bending observations. Although laboratory measurements impose formidable technical challenges, astronomical observations of compact spinning objects offer promising avenues to constrain or falsify the proposed framework.
item.dc:creator: Zhiguang Tan, Shengjie Wang, Hua Zheng

item.title: Gravitational Particle Production and Locality of the Wavefunction-Squared
item.description: arXiv:2611.13864v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that no particle production due to the background geometry implies the locality of the wavefunction-squared for free heavy masses on expanding cosmologies. On global de Sitter of odd dimensions these two stem from the same identity, whereas in the Poincare patch neither occur under any condition. These two phenomena both depend on the behaviour of the out modes at far future and we show that they almost always come together for systems with an out mode that has a phase with separated time and momentum dependency at far future. This will be true for most expanding cosmologies. We comment on how the discussion can be connected to Green's functions and on some previous results in the literature that are seemingly contrary to our conclusions.
item.dc:creator: Emine \c{S}eyma Kutluk

item.title: Landau Theory of Black-Brane Phase Transitions from Kasner Singularities
item.description: arXiv:2611.14075v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a Landau theory of a continuous black-brane phase transition using the geometry of the black-hole interior. The normal phase has a Reissner--Nordstr\"om Cauchy horizon, whereas the scalarized phase ends at a Kasner singularity. A conserved radial charge determines the grand potential from either endpoint and permits a direct phase comparison. At the critical point, we show analytically that the quadratic correction to the conserved radial charge vanishes. Using the inverse Kasner scalar velocity as an interior order parameter, we then construct a Landau potential whose coefficients are determined entirely from the terminal singularity. The Iyer--Wald first law relates this potential to the conventional boundary Landau theory and fixes its quartic coefficient. For two models with different scalar self-interactions, the resulting theory predicts the critical scaling of the Kasner order parameter and the grand-potential difference between the phases, in agreement with fully backreacted numerical solutions.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Da Lyu

item.title: Relativistic tidal response and mode excitation in neutron-star binaries
item.description: arXiv:2611.14243v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tidal excitation links gravitational-wave emission to the internal dynamics of neutron stars. We study the dynamical tidal response of nonrotating stars with composition stratification, elastic crusts and possible first-order phase transitions. Using analytical Mano--Suzuki--Takasugi exterior solutions, we match stellar perturbations to an effective field theory and extract the poles and residues of the relativistic tidal response. Over the inspiral band, this response is accurately approximated by a sum of harmonic oscillators, as in Newtonian theory, each specified by a frequency $\omega_\alpha$ and a mode-specific tidal deformability $\lambda_\alpha$, or equivalently a tidal overlap $I_\alpha$. We couple these oscillators to relativistic effective-one-body dynamics, including gravitational redshift and frame dragging, to follow mode excitation and gravitational-wave emission. A decomposition into driven and free oscillations gives analytical mode amplitudes accurate to a few percent during inspiral. We also reconstruct the time-dependent crustal strain. In a representative $1.20+1.50\,M_\odot$ hadronic--hybrid binary, gravity, interface and shear modes produce a gravitational-wave phase shift of $\lesssim10^{-2}\,{\rm rad}$. Despite this small phase shift, gravity-mode excitation can overstrain the crust near its base, while the lowest shear mode produces widespread overstrain.
item.dc:creator: Yong Gao, Jan Steinhoff

item.title: Brans-Dicke Theory with $\Lambda {\ensuremath >} 0$: Black Holes and Large Scale Structures
item.description: arXiv:1505.02375v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A step-by-step approach is followed to study cosmic structures in the context of Brans-Dicke theory with positive cosmological constant $\Lambda$ and parameter $\omega$. First, it is shown that regular stationary black-hole solutions not only have constant Brans-Dicke field $\phi$, but can exist only for $\omega=\infty$, which forces the theory to coincide with the General Relativity. Generalizations of the theory in order to evade this black-hole no-hair theorem are presented. It is also shown that in the absence of a stationary cosmological event horizon in the asymptotic region, a stationary black hole horizon can support a non-trivial Brans-Dicke hair. Even more importantly, it is shown next, that the presence of a stationary cosmological event horizon rules out any regular stationary solution, appropriate for the description of a star. Thus, to describe a star one has to assume that there is no such stationary horizon in the faraway asymptotic region. Under this implicit assumption generic spherical cosmic structures are studied perturbatively and is shown that only for $\omega>0$ or $\omega\lesssim -5$ their predicted maximum sizes are consistent with observations. We also point out how, many of the conclusions of this work differ qualitatively from the $\Lambda=0$ spacetimes.
item.dc:creator: Sourav Bhattacharya, Konstantinos F. Dialektopoulos, Antonio Enea Romano, Theodore N. Tomaras

item.title: Wormhole geometries in Einstein-aether theory
item.description: arXiv:2511.00825v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the first analysis of traversable wormholes within the framework of Einstein-aether theory. We show that the corresponding field equations admit three distinct wormhole geometries, obtained by adopting three different classes of combinations for the aether coupling constants. We examine the null and weak energy conditions for three types of wormhole shape functions. Our results show that, for appropriate choices of the wormhole parameters and the coupling constants of the theory, these wormhole geometries can satisfy the null and weak energy conditions. Furthermore, we find that the satisfaction of these energy conditions is restricted to certain ranges of the aether coupling constants, which can be interpreted as constraints arising from the requirement of avoiding exotic matter. However, these ranges are incompatible with the constraints imposed by physical considerations and observational bounds. This suggests that, as in Einstein gravity, exotic matter is necessary to support traversable wormhole geometries in Einstein-aether theory.
item.dc:creator: Hanif Golchin, Hamid R. Bakhtiarizadeh, Mohammad Reza Mehdizadeh

item.title: Impact on Inferred Neutron Star Equation of State due to Nonlinear Hydrodynamics, Background Spin, and Relativity
item.description: arXiv:2602.04951v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Tidal interaction is a unique, detectable signature in gravitational wave signals from inspiraling binary neutron stars (BNSs), which can be used to constrain the neutron star (NS) equation of state (EoS). The tidal interaction is resonantly amplified as the orbital frequency approaches the NS fundamental mode (f-mode) frequency. It has been shown that the exclusion of tidal resonance in parameter estimation leads to a significant bias in the inferred NS tidal deformability and hence the NS EoS [Pratten et al. PRL 129, 081102 (2022)]. The strength and location of tidal resonance depend sensitively on the f-mode frequency, which is typically modeled using its universal relation with the tidal deformability that is derived for an isolated, non-spinning NS assuming only linear fluid perturbations. In a BNS inspiral, the f-mode frequency can be corrected by at least three known effects: nonlinear hydrodynamics, background spin, and relativity. We use Hamiltonian Monte Carlo simulations to estimate the systematic bias on tidal deformability when each frequency correction is ignored. Our study considers both loud, individual events and the stacking of a population of detections. Both scenarios are expected when the next-generation detectors are available with a sensitivity level increased by about an order of magnitude.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Classical and Quantum Gravity, Volume 43, Number 12, Pages 125011, 2026
item.dc:creator: Joseph Bretz, Hang Yu

item.title: Global existence for a Fritz John equation in expanding FLRW spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2603.02307v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the family of semilinear wave equations $\square_{\mathbf{g}_p}\phi=(\partial_t\phi)^2$, on fixed expanding FLRW spacetimes, having $\mathbb{R}^3$ spatial slices and undergoing a power law expansion, with scale factor $a(t)=t^p$, $0< p \le 1$. This is a natural generalization to a non-stationary background of a famous Fritz John ''blow-up'' equation in $\mathbb{R}^{1+3}$ (corresponding to $p=0$, i.e. the case in which $\mathbf{g}_0$ is the Minkowski metric). While, in Minkowski spacetime ($p=0$), non-trivial solutions to this equation are known to diverge in finite time, here we prove that, on the referred FLRW backgrounds ($0<p\leq 1$), sufficiently small, smooth, and compactly supported initial data yield global-in-time solutions to the future. Previous work, co-authored by the first two authors, considered accelerated expanding spacetimes ($p>1$) and relied on the integrability of the inverse of the scale factor to establish future global well-posedness. In the current work, where such an integrability condition is lacking, we rely on a vector field method that captures and combines dispersive estimates with the spacetime expansion to control the solution and suppress the nonlinear blow-up mechanism. To achieve this, we commute the Laplace-Beltrami operator with a boosts-free subset of the Poincar\'e algebra and employ Klainerman-Sideris types of inequalities. Our strategy is general and is developed to handle the non-stationary nature of FLRW spacetimes. While we focus solely on this Fritz John type of equation, which serves as a prototype to study blow-up of non-linear waves, our approach provides a rigorous proof of the regularizing effects of spacetime expansion and can be exploited for a wider range of applications and nonlinearities.
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao L. Costa, Jes\'us Oliver, Flavio Rossetti

item.title: Probing soft signals of gravitational-wave memory with space-based interferometers
item.description: arXiv:2603.28689v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gravitational-wave displacement memory is a remarkable, ubiquitous prediction of general relativity that has not yet been detected. Unlike the oscillatory components of gravitational waveforms, displacement memory is associated with soft gravitons and provides the leading low-frequency observable of its parent event. Analogous soft signals may also be associated with velocity and integrated-displacement memory. The simple, universal spectral shapes of soft waveforms provide effective templates for matched filtering and parameter estimation. In this paper, we investigate the detection prospects for such soft memory signals with future space-based laser interferometers. As realistic examples, we examine the infrared spectral features of gravitational waves from moderately relativistic nonspinning compact binary scattering and comparable-mass quasicircular, nonprecessing black hole mergers. In both cases, the low-frequency spectrum can be described by a soft displacement-memory waveform with finite-frequency corrections. Using the adopted instrumental-noise models, simulated Bayesian parameter-estimation analyses show that a single LISA-like detector can constrain the memory amplitude and arrival time for signals with matched-filter signal-to-noise ratios of order 10. Big Bang Observer (BBO) Stage 1 could measure null displacement memory from sufficiently loud stellar-mass compact binary mergers. We also evaluate the detectability of an idealized stochastic background of soft displacement-memory signals. These results establish gravitational-wave bursts with memory as concrete targets for space-based interferometers.
item.dc:creator: Yan Cao, Yong-Liang Ma, Yong Tang

item.title: Superdilations at Schwarzschild null infinity and beyond
item.description: arXiv:2605.26296v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Relying on the definition of asymptotic conformal Killing horizons, the generators of asymptotic conformal symmetries at future null infinity in Schwarzschild space-time is computed. Supertranslations and superdilations are generated by two independent functions on the sphere, and the generators close an enlarged algebra with respect to the BMS one. For a generic asymptotically flat space-time, the superdilations Iyer-Wald charge is non-trivial but divergent at the boundaries of null infinity, where its growth rate is fixed by the asymptotic values of the Bondi mass aspect. Such a rate equals the monopole supertranslation charge, for which antipodal matching is well posed and trivially satisfied in the Schwarzschild geometry, where, furthermore, only the global dilation mode contributes. Its growth reflects the explicit time dependence of the generator rather than radiation. The effect of superdilations on a pair of celestial observers is an angle-dependent dilation rate, related to the local density of the charge.
item.dc:creator: Marco Refuto

item.title: Long-term 3+1 simulations of primordial black hole formation during radiation domination
item.description: arXiv:2608.13206v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop an efficient three-dimensional numerical-relativity framework for primordial black-hole (PBH) formation from superhorizon curvature perturbations in a radiation-dominated Universe. We implement flux-conservative relativistic hydrodynamics in the adaptive-mesh-refinement code GRChombo and introduce a cosmologically scaled Gamma-driver that allows the cosmic-time step to grow in proportion to the scale factor. For a representative long-term simulation, the scaled driver preserves the apparent-horizon mass evolution and constraint behavior while reducing the number of coarse-level advances by a factor of approximately $94$ relative to the standard driver. We also construct a conformal-time version of the moving-puncture gauge as a consistency check. Applying the framework to a spherical Gaussian curvature profile, we find a collapse threshold $\mu_c \simeq 0.7958$ and approximate critical mass scaling, consistent with previous spherically symmetric results. We further fit the late-time PBH mass growth to the Zel'dovich--Novikov accretion law, demonstrating that the code can follow both near-critical collapse and long-term post-formation evolution in three dimensions. The framework provides a foundation for future studies of PBH formation beyond spherical symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Zhuan Ning, Rong-Gen Cai, Shao-Jiang Wang, Chul-Moon Yoo

item.title: No-Go Theorem for Phantom Crossing in Scalar-Tensor Gravity with Non-Minimal Derivative Coupling and Soft Scale-Invariance Breaking
item.description: arXiv:2610.14354v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI 2024) reveal a preference for dynamical dark energy with an equation of state parameter crossing the phantom divide ($w < -1$) at low redshifts. We investigate whether this phantom crossing can be realized within scale-invariant scalar-tensor theories featuring non-minimal derivative coupling (NMDC) between the scalar field and the Einstein tensor. Employing the effective field theory of dark energy formalism, we systematically derive the ghost-free and gradient stability conditions, and examine their compatibility with the swampland conjectures from quantum gravity. We establish three rigorous no-go theorems demonstrating that: (i)~phantom crossing necessitates $\xi_{\text{eff}} < 0$, directly violating the no-ghost stability requirement $\xi_{\text{eff}} > 0$; (ii)~the swampland de Sitter and distance conjectures independently obstruct phantom crossing; and (iii)~these theoretical obstructions are mutually reinforcing. Our results show that scale-invariant NMDC models cannot account for the DESI preference for $w < -1$, providing robust theoretical guidance for dark energy model building beyond this class.

item.title: Probing parity-breaking black-hole geometry with extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
item.description: arXiv:2610.25291v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the gravitational-wave signatures of equatorial reflection symmetry breaking in extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) around a parity-violating conformal Kerr black hole. For the circular-orbit branch connected to equatorial Kerr orbits, we derive the dynamics through second order in the dimensionless deformation parameter $\varepsilon$ and construct adiabatic inspirals and gravitational-wave signals using a mass-quadrupole prescription. Equatorial reflection maps $\varepsilon$ to $-\varepsilon$, making the polar displacement odd and the orbital frequency and energy even in the deformation. The induced first harmonic has a small direct contribution for the configurations studied, while second-order dynamical corrections accumulate over many cycles to produce appreciable dephasing. We find that rapid black-hole rotation enhances these phase effects and the associated noise-weighted waveform mismatch. For a one-year inspiral of a $10M_\odot$ object into a $10^6M_\odot$ black hole with $a/M=0.9$ and viewing inclination $\iota=2\pi/3$, the fixed-parameter mismatch reaches the comparison benchmark $\mathcal M=0.01$ at approximately $\varepsilon=10^{-3}$, without optimization over time, phase, or Kerr parameters. A single-parameter Fisher analysis also indicates improved local sensitivity to $\varepsilon$ at high spin. These results connect the reflection properties of the circular branch to accumulated source-phase effects and complement tests of propagation birefringence.
item.dc:creator: Zhen-Bo Wu, Qing Ou, Peng-Cheng Li

item.title: Deflating the Spacetime-Matter Dichotomy
item.description: arXiv:2512.10775v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we analyse scalar-tensor theories-specific instances of which include mainstream inflation and dark energy models-in light of the spacetime-matter dichotomy. We argue that it is difficult to categorise the scalar fields as either a pure aspect of the spacetime structure or a pure form of matter, by focusing on the Jordan vs Einstein frames of these theories. We present and evaluate various interpretational options available, concluding that the spacetime-matter dichotomy becomes untenable in this context. At the same time, the ontological and conceptual category of spacetime can be decoupled from that of gravity, with the latter remaining viable in the context of scalar-tensor theories.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Ferreiro, Alex Fleuren, Niels C. M. Martens

item.title: Gravitational open effective field theory of inflation
item.description: arXiv:2512.21234v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a gravitational open extension of the effective field theory of inflation in the Schwinger-Keldysh framework. While physical symmetries allow many open operators in the Schwinger-Keldysh action, most of them overconstrain the equations of motion, yielding inconsistent dynamics. We identify a minimal open operator compatible with propagating scalar and tensor modes and build a local gravitational action, recovering known dissipative models of inflation.
item.dc:creator: Perseas Christodoulidis, Jinn-Ouk Gong

item.title: Causal Order Cannot Be An Observable
item.description: arXiv:2605.25302v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent developments in the formalisation of quantum causal structures have made it possible to test and compare hypotheses about causal structure empirically, rather than being a-priori assumptions. Such differences in causal structure may be leveraged to distinguish between the processes they belong to, akin to distinguishing between quantum states known to belong to different eigenspaces of an observable. So how far this analogy can be pushed? Can causal order be interpreted as a kind of observable? Can it be measured? To this end we construct a completely operational definition of observables in terms of `discrimination tasks'. This begins with some base set of classes (analogous to a quantum observable's eigenspaces) before we impose three conditions on how these classes relate under discrimination tasks. These conditions recover the properties of a standard observable, letting us apply this definition to non-state entities such as quantum processes, which naturally encode causal structure. The first of these conditions (1) asserts that a member of any class is perfectly distinguishable from a member of any other class -- for states, this implies conditions (2) and (3), but we show this does not hold automatically for processes (or indeed channels). By analysing classes of quantum processes having strict causal orders, we find causal classes which are sharp but violate condition 2 (but not 3), and classes which are likewise sharp and violate condition 3 (but not 2). This implies that causal order cannot be an observable.
